text: If two straight-lines cut one another then they make the vertically opposite angles equal to one another.  For let the two straight-lines $AB$ and $CD$ cut one another at the point $E$. I say that  angle $AEC$ is equal to (angle) $DEB$, and (angle) $CEB$ to (angle) $AED$.
For since the straight-line $AE$ stands on the straight-line $CD$, making the angles $CEA$ and $AED$, the (sum of the) angles $CEA$ and $AED$ is thus equal to two right-angles [Prop.~1.13].
assertion: the sum of angles CEA and AED equals two right-angles

text: Again, since the straight-line $DE$ stands on the straight-line $AB$, making the angles $AED$ and $DEB$, the (sum of the) angles $AED$ and $DEB$ is thus equal to two right-angles [Prop.~1.13].
assertion: the sum of angles AED and DEB equals two right-angles

text: But (the sum of) $CEA$ and $AED$ was also shown (to be) equal to two right-angles.
